To find the **greatest common divisor (GCD)** of the three numbers $ 3339 $, $ 2961 $, and $ 1491 $, we can use the **Euclidean algorithm**, which is an efficient method for computing the GCD of two numbers. Since the GCD of more than two numbers can be found by iteratively computing the GCD of pairs, we proceed step by step.

---

### Step 1: Find GCD of 3339 and 2961

We apply the Euclidean algorithm:

$$
\begin{align*}
3339 \div 2961 &= 1 \text{ remainder } 378 \\
2961 \div 378 &= 7 \text{ remainder } 315 \\
378 \div 315 &= 1 \text{ remainder } 63 \\
315 \div 63 &= 5 \text{ remainder } 0
\end{align*}
$$

So, $ \gcd(3339, 2961) = 63 $.

---

### Step 2: Find GCD of 63 and 1491

Now we compute $ \gcd(63, 1491) $:

$$
\begin{align*}
1491 \div 63 &= 23 \text{ remainder } 42 \\
63 \div 42 &= 1 \text{ remainder } 21 \\
42 \div 21 &= 2 \text{ remainder } 0
\end{align*}
$$

So, $ \gcd(63, 1491) = 21 $.

---

### Final Result:

Therefore, the GCD of all three numbers $ 3339 $, $ 2961 $, and $ 1491 $ is:

$$
\boxed{21}
$$
